title: Port-worker solidarity march during ATI strike in Antofagasta
location: Antofagasta: port plaza to Plaza de la Revolución
organizer: Three port unions at Antofagasta Terminal Internacional (ATI), with worker/student solidarity groups
participants_original: La Izquierda Diario reports nearly 200 people
threshold_50_evidence: The opened report estimates nearly 200 participants; above the 50-person threshold, attributed to this activist outlet.

location.summary: Route from port plaza to Plaza de la Revolución, Antofagasta.

organizer.summary: Three ATI port unions called the march; workers, students and social groups joined.

demands.summary: Immediate dispute concerned ATI collective-contract clauses, wages, training and working conditions.

participants.summary: Nearly 200 participants reported by La Izquierda Diario; single outlet estimate.

protester_violence.summary: Union leader called for peaceful demonstration; no participant violence in reviewed account.

state_response.summary: No response stated in reviewed passage; unknown.

notes: Discrete October street march while the port unions were on strike from September. S009 documents strike onset/settlement timeline; do not treat all strike days as public assemblies. The report centers on ATI collective-bargaining issues, including wages/training and contract clauses; it also contains broader political solidarity speech.
open_questions: Does the labor dispute constitute eligible target/category under official codebook?
Independent contemporaneous attendance estimate not opened.

title: First-anniversary assembly at Plaza Baquedano / Plaza Italia, Santiago
participants_original: Government estimate reported by BioBioChile: about 25,000; separate bicycle flow ~10,000 not added
threshold_50_evidence: A government estimate of about 25,000 at Plaza Baquedano is reported in S001 and echoed by the S003 rolling update; S002 independently confirms thousands without a numeric figure. Bicycle estimate is a separate possibly overlapping flow and is excluded.

start_date.summary: Both contemporaneous sources report 18 October anniversary gathering.

demands.summary: Social-demand banners and pandemic-related domestic discontent reported; exact list unresolved. The encouragement to vote is a political-process cue, not proof of all participants’ demands.

participants.summary: Government estimate ~25,000; S002 says thousands but no count. Separate ~10,000 cyclists not added.

threshold_50.summary: Multiple descriptions of thousands and government estimate ~25,000.

protester_violence.summary: Chronology describes violent incidents by actors with varying attribution; cannot attribute to main crowd.

state_response.summary: Police dispersal and arrests reported, but source timelines include citywide actions; extent toward this assembly not fully bounded.

notes: Anniversary gathering with social-demand banners and encouragement to participate in the 25 October constitutional plebiscite. Specific demands and the event target are not itemized. Citywide chronology sources contain distinct groups/incidents; violence is not generalized to this gathering.
open_questions: Which specific demand and state target correspond to the main assembly, distinct from nearby groups/incidents?

threshold_50_evidence: Cooperativa reports about 1,500 people marched in Rancagua on 18 October.

demands.summary: Not individually specified for this march.

title: Anniversary assembly and march in Temuco
location: Temuco, Plaza Janequeo and central streets
organizer: Asamblea de Mujeres del Ngulumapu (reported by S007)
participants_original: Conflicting local estimates: approximately 300 (Cooperativa) and about 700 (La Izquierda Diario)
threshold_50_evidence: Both opened reports place the gathering well above 50: S003 estimates ~300; S007 reports ~700. Range records incompatible estimates, not a statistical confidence interval.

start_date.summary: Both date Temuco action to 19 October; S007 published the next day.

location.summary: Plaza Janequeo/ex-Armas and central streets in Temuco.

organizer.summary: Asamblea de Mujeres del Ngulumapu reportedly organized call; social/political organizations participated.

demands.summary: Speeches called for prosecution/punishment for human-rights violations and a sovereign constituent assembly.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence described in reviewed narrative.

state_response.summary: Police dispersed march with tear gas/water-cannon vehicles.

notes: Published 20 October by La Izquierda Diario about the 19 October action; this source reports organizer and demands for prosecution/punishment of human-rights violators and a sovereign constituent assembly. S003 reports a distinct estimate of ~300. Activist outlet framing; count range remains attributed. No continuity with the 18 October Santiago assembly is inferred.
open_questions: Can a further contemporaneous opened source reconcile estimates?
Review classification of police-brutality / constituent-process demands.

state_response.summary: No response established for this site in reviewed passage.

title: Anniversary march toward Parliament in Valparaíso
location: Valparaíso, Plaza Victoria and central route toward Parliament
threshold_50_evidence: Cooperativa reports about 3,000 in Valparaíso; 24Horas confirms march route and describes local incidents but gives no count.

start_date.summary: Both reports date Valparaíso/anniversary actions to 19 October.

location.summary: Plaza Victoria and route toward Parliament, Valparaíso.

participants.summary: About 3,000; not a pooled national estimate.

demands.summary: Specific demands not stated; route to Parliament alone does not specify demand.

protester_violence.summary: Source reports varied actors and incidents; cannot attribute broadly.

state_response.summary: Police repelled some marchers near Parliament.

notes: City-level march; 24Horas describes a route toward Parliament and police repelling part of the crowd, but demands and organizers are not specified. It also describes property damage and clashes by differently described actors; these are not generalized to all marchers.
open_questions: Specific demand and organizer evidence for the Valparaíso action?
